**Top‑5 highest‑grossing animated feature films (worldwide, unadjusted for inflation) – 2025 data**

| Rank (by worldwide gross) | Film (Year) | Approx. Worldwide Gross* | Director(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **The Lion King** (2019) – photorealistic CGI remake | **≈ $1.66 billion** | **Jon Favreau** (sole director) |
| **2** | **Frozen II** (2019) | **≈ $1.45 billion** | **Chris Buck** & **Jennifer Lee** (co‑directors) |
| **3** | **The Super Mario Bros. Movie** (2023) | **≈ $1.36 billion** | **Aaron Horvath** & **Michael Jelenic** (co‑directors) |
| **4** | **Frozen** (2013) | **≈ $1.28 billion** | **Chris Buck** & **Jennifer Lee** (co‑directors) |
| **5** | **Minions** (2015) | **≈ $1.16 billion** | **Pierre Coffin** (director) – co‑directed by **Kyle Balda** |

\*Figures are rounded to the nearest $10 million and reflect the totals reported by Box Office Mojo / The Numbers up to October 2025.  

### Quick notes on the directors

| Film | Director(s) | Notable facts |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| **The Lion King** (2019) | Jon Favreau | First major Disney “live‑action/CGI” remake; Favreau also produced the film. |
| **Frozen II** | Chris Buck & Jennifer Lee | Buck previously co‑directed *Frozen* (2013); Lee became the first female director of a Disney animated feature to top $1 billion. |
| **The Super Mario Bros. Movie** | Aaron Horvath & Michael Jelenic | Both are longtime collaborators on Warner Bros. Animation series (*Teen Titans Go!*, *The Amazing World of Gumball*). |
| **Frozen** | Chris Buck & Jennifer Lee | The pair earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature. |
| **Minions** | Pierre Coffin (director) – co‑directed by Kyle Balda | Coffin also directed the *Despicable Me* series; Balda is a long‑time Illumination animator and co‑director on several Illumination projects. |

These are the directors responsible for the five animated movies that have earned the most money worldwide as of late 2025.
